The Congress has been at the forefront of protests against the BJP government over alleged vote theft and for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged manipulation of voter rolls. According to the party, marches in many parts of the country would begin or conclude at statues of B R Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi with a reading of the Preamble and an oath to protect the Constitution. articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that contempt petitions and other applications on the controversy surrounding the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon pillar on the Thirupparankundram hill will be listed on November 27. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi was informed by counsels appearing for the matter that multiple contempt petitions and applications have been filed on the issue and the court may hear it urgently. "Everything will be listed tomorrow," the bench said. On Wednesday, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it. The apex court, while refusing to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings, said it will hear such a plea if filed. It said the registry will verify the filing of applications for permission to light the lamp, including contempt petitions, and the court will see if they can be listed on Thursday or Friday. For decades, the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes. articles.title: Government ‘jealous’ that 27-year-old invited to Oxford: Abhijeet Dipke on Saurav Das being stopped from flying
articles.summary: Nagpur: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday alleged that CJP co-convenor Saurav Das was prevented from travelling to the London School of Economics and Oxford University because the government was “jealous” that the 27-year-old had been invited to the prestigious institutions. Speaking to the media after visiting Deekshabhoomi ahead of their ‘Save Democracy, Save Constitution’ rally in Nagpur, Dipke said he, Das and co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka had received invitations and decided that Das would travel to the United Kingdom . “We had decided that Ashutosh and I would travel across Maharashtra because there is a drought in the state, and we wanted to visit the affected areas. We had decided that Saurav Das would go to the London School of Economics and Oxford. But when he went to the airport, he was stopped,” Dipke said. Saurav Das not allowed to travel abroad as Mumbai Police issued LOC against him: Centre tells Delhi High Court Das on Wednesday approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped from flying to the UK for an event at Oxford University, where he was slated to speak on the “cockroach movement”. Later, the Ministry of External Affairs said Das had been issued a show-cause notice to explain discrepancies in his place of birth on his passport following inputs from relevant authorities. “I think there is some insecurity somewhere… I think there is someone in our country who feels that only he should go on a world tour. Perhaps they felt a little jealous that a 27-year-old was being invited to Oxford University,” Dipke said. The CJP founder alleged that some people were jealous because they were not being invited anywhere. They were perhaps wondering how Das was receiving so much international recognition, he said. Dipke said the Jantar Mantar movement, which catapulted CJP into the mainstream, succeeded by following the path shown by Babasaheb Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. “But there are some big narcissists in our country who think that not just the country, but the entire world should revolve around them, and that only they should go on world tours,” he said. Asked about his allegations that CJP leaders were being pressured, Dipke said the government’s approach was to find ways to “crush the voices against it”. Rattled by CJP movement's success, Centre stopped Saurav Das from flying to UK: Abhijeet Dipke Dipke said the government could take such action but should not forget that, while it held power, the Constitution given to the country by Babasaheb Ambedkar was on their side. “The Constitution is on our side. Power may be yours, but the Constitution is ours. The Constitution belongs to 140 crore people. Whenever a tyrant in power tries to snatch away people’s rights, it is this very Constitution of Dr Babasaheb that will protect them, just as it has protected us,” he said. Dipke alleged that Ashutosh Ranka had been kept in Tihar Jail for eight days for waving the Tricolour. articles.title: 1994 Gopalganj DM's murder: SC quashes Bihar govt order granting remission to gangster-turned-MP Anand Mohan
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday quashed the Bihar government's decision to grant premature release to former MP Anand Mohan from the life term awarded to him in a case related to leading a mob that lynched the then Gopalganj District Magistrate in 1994. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held the State has failed to justify the legitimate public purpose for the selective remission, holding that the amended policy was manifestly arbitrary and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution. "Grant of premature release to Mohan in such circumstances is indefensible and unsustainable in law," Justice Datta said, reading out excerpts of the judgment. The court declared the notification of April 10, 2023 as unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative and thus set aside. The order of April 24, 2023 granting premature release to gangster-turned-politician Mohan was also quashed. The bench directed Mohan to surrender before the prison authorities within a month. The court directed any future consideration of the plea for premature release of Mohan should be undertaken only after giving an opportunity of hearing to Umadevi Krishnaiah, wife of deceased IAS officer G Krishnaiah. In an epilogue, the bench emphasised in cases of premature mature, Article 21 cannot be considered as one sided guarantee, intended for the convict, who has served substantially long period of imprisonment as the right equally encompasses the right of the victims and the family members. The court's judgment came on a writ petition filed by Umadevi Krishnaiah, who then questioned the decision of the then Nitish Kumar government to amend the prison rules and subsequent release of Mohan on April 24, 2023. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra argued the matter on behalf of the petitioner. Her plea contended the Bihar government has specially brought about an amendment on April 10, 2023 to the Bihar Prison Manual with retrospective effect, in order to ensure that the convict Mohan be granted benefit of remission. "The said amendment of April 10, 2023 is against the notification of December 10, 2002 as well as against the public policy and has resulted in demoralisation of the Civil Servants in the state," it said. The plea also stated that life imprisonment, when awarded as a substitute for death penalty, has to be carried out strictly as directed by the court and it would be beyond the application of remission. "The convict here is a politically influential person and has committed the murder of a serving IAS officer, while himself being an MLA. He enjoys political support and has several criminal cases pending against him," it also claimed. The plea also said the grant of remission to Mohan was in contravention of the notification of December 10, 2002 which was applicable on the date of conviction i.e. on October 5, 2007. "Therefore, order dated 24.04.2023 by the State of Bihar is violation of notification dated 10.12.2002 as well as in contravention of judgments of the apex court," it said. The plea submitted that life imprisonment handed down to the gangster-turned-politician meant incarceration for his entire natural course of life as in his case, he was awarded death penalty on October 5, 2007 by the trial court which was commuted to rigorous life imprisonment by the Patna High Court on December 10, 2008 and confirmed by the Supreme Court on July 10, 2012. Mohan was released from Saharsa jail on April 27, 2023. Her plea also referred to Rule 481(1)(c) of Bihar Prison Manual, 2012, which provided that convicts whose death sentence has been commuted to life sentence will be eligible for consideration of remission only after completion of 20 years of sentence. "Mohan has served only 14 years of incarceration and therefore, he is not eligible to be considered for remission as per rule," it said. A 1985-batch IAS officer Krishnaiah hailed from Telangana. He was just 37-year-old and was posted as district magistrate of Gopalganj. He was beaten to death by a mob in 1994 when his vehicle tried to overtake the funeral procession of gangster Chhotan Shukla in Muzaffarpur district.

articles.title: Karunadotsava | Tracing Kannada theatre’s journey from folk canopies to modern stages
articles.summary: Kannada has a rich tradition of folk theatre that dates back several centuries. References to theatrical performances like Sri Krishna Parijatha, Yakshagana, Sannata and Doddata, which blend music with narration and dialogue, can be found in numerous documents. All that performers needed was a raised platform and canopy overhead. Around mid-19th century, touring Parsi theatre companies from Mumbai had a significant influence on Kannada theatre. Inspired by British companies that staged English plays in Mumbai, Parsis started commercial theatre companies performing plays based on historical characters and Indianised versions of Shakespeare. Touring Marathi companies followed suit. Some of these troupes were invited by Wodeyar kings to perform at Mysore palace. While popularity of Marathi and Hindustani performances challenged Kannadiga pride and led to establishment of Kannada theatre companies in north Karnataka , royal patronage helped theatre flourish in the south. Sri Chamarajendra Karnataka Nataka Sabha was established under the auspices of the palace. Karunadotsava | The making of Karnataka: A walk through centuries of history Karunadotsava | Kannada writers every Indian literature lover should know Initially, these commercial companies staged plays based on mythology and translations of Sanskrit plays. Their attention soon turned to Shakespeare. While some adaptations simply gave characters Indian names, others modified plots to suit Indian audiences. The performances were marked by grand sets and scenery, loud music, glittering costumes and jewellery. Since music was crucial to plays, actors had to be trained singers. In first quarter of the 20th century, acting became more subtle. Women began playing female roles, long been performed by men. Commercial theatre reached its zenith with Gubbi company. Not all commercial theatre companies could survive competition from cinema. Some of them remain active even today, on a much smaller scale. Karunadotsava | Sandalwood: From regional roots to global possibilities Karunadotsava | ‘Kannada-Kannadi’ holds up a mirror to Karnataka’s history With emergence of Western-educated middle class, a demand arose for new kind of theatre. They preferred realistic plays that held a mirror to contemporary society. T P Kailasam and Sriranga were among founders of this realistic school. Kailasam wrote reformist social plays that addressed evils like dowry and oppressive customs. His witty comments, use of irony and realistic, spoken language appealed to middle-class audience. Sriranga’s plays covered a larger canvas and included elaborate stage directions and suggestions on lighting and technique. A parallel development was emergence of poetic drama and literary adaptations of Greek drama and Shakespeare by Kannada writers. Though rich in literary value, not all these plays were successful on stage. Samsa, who wrote historical plays based on lives and reigns of Wadiyar kings, occupies unique place among early modernists. Absurdist drama, influenced by post-World War despair in the West, dominated the stage for a while in the 1960s. Playwrights occupied centre stage during this period. Among playwrights whose works were widely staged in the last few decades are G B Joshi, P Lankesh, Chandrashekar Patil, Girish Karnad, Chandrashekhara Kambara and H S Shivaprakash. B V Karanth, Prasanna and K V Akshara are among directors who turned playwrights. Karanth, among the first graduates of National School of Drama (NSD), Delhi, revolutionised Kannada theatre with Total Theatre, which blended classical Sanskrit and Western traditions with regional folk arts and street theatre. He used music as an integral part of the narrative. Benaka, the group he founded, continues to stage his successful productions. Karunadotsava | Keeping Bengaluru’s Kannada cultural identity alive, one place at a time Karunadotsava: 3 books that will take you into the world of Kannada storytelling With the founding of Samudaya, Prasanna, along with C G Krishnaswamy (CGK), transformed theatre into a mass movement rooted in progressive values and social commitment. Through its units across state, Samudaya has produced a number of progressive plays. With around 50 graduates from NSD, Kannada theatre witnessed a series of new productions from the 1970s that were more sophisticated in content, stage and costume design. Bertolt Brecht’s concept of epic theatre has been a major influence on many modern playwrights. The close affinity between epic theatre and our own folk traditions has encouraged playwrights to borrow techniques from folk theatre to depict contemporary issues. H S Shivaprakash’s Manteswami Katha Prasanga and Maadari Maadiah , which celebrate two great folk heroes while addressing contemporary issues are classic examples of this. Ninasam Theatre Institute, founded by K V Subbanna at Heggodu, introduced a one-year theatre training course in Kannada, modelled on NSD programme. Artistes trained in the course gained practical experience by being part of the travelling repertory, Tirugata, for a year. This made theatre training more accessible to Kannada-speaking youngsters from poor backgrounds. With the involvement of NSD — and Ninasam — trained directors, amateur theatre groups, too, have been encouraged to become more professional. The increase in the number of theatre groups led to the creation of more theatre spaces. In Bengaluru, availability of a fully equipped theatre like Ranga Shankara has given a new lease of life to smaller groups. Since the number of new plays being written could not meet demands of the numerous theatre groups eager to stage new productions, adaptations of novels, short stories and other literary works for stage began to gain popularity. One such production, which made history in recent years, is the stage adaptation of Kuvempu’s masterpiece, Malegalalli Madumagalu , directed by C Basavalingaiah. This 9-hour-long, all-night play was performed at 3 venues. Solo theatre performance is another major genre that emerged in recent times. Since most performers and directors in this genre are women, it has provided a platform to voice women’s issues. Through the establishment of government-funded Rangayana repertories in different parts of the state, beginning with the one in Mysuru under B V Karanth, the government has tried to promote Kannada theatre. articles.summary: Mumbai: A special court here has ordered that an accused in the actor Tiger Shroff attack case be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) after it was confirmed that he was 17 years old. The accused, who was one of the shooters, will be produced before the JJB and be sent to a correctional home instead of jail. Earlier this month, the boy’s father filed an application stating that his son was a minor and should therefore not be produced before the regular court. Tiger Shroff returns to stage, performs in Mumbai weeks after shooting incident On Wednesday, the prosecution submitted his documents, including the school leaving certificate and birth certificate, showing that the boy was born on November 30, 2008. The court then ordered that he be produced before the JJB. “From the inquiry conducted, the accused is found to be a ‘child’ on the date of the incident. Therefore, it is necessary to produce him before the Juvenile Justice Board,” Special Judge S R Navander said. Two shooters fired five rounds at Shroff’s car as he was leaving a football ground in Mumbai’s Juhu on October 18. While the 36-year-old actor escaped largely unhurt, his car driver and a bystander, who is a vlogger, were injured. Members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang had claimed responsibility for the firing. Police have named jailed gangster Bishnoi’s aide Anil Pandit as a wanted accused in the case. The minor accused was arrested the next day in Rajasthan.

articles.title: Mumbai 26/11 terror attack survivor ‘Baby Moshe’ pursuing rabbinical studies in New York
articles.summary: Mumbai: Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy popularly known as ‘Baby Moshe’ who survived the 2008 Nariman House terror attack that claimed his parents’ lives, is pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and aspires to become a rabbi like his father. Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, one of the places targeted by Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists during the November 26, 2008 attacks , said he met Moshe two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference in New York. “The conference was attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world, and Moshe was also present,” Kozlovsky said, showing a photograph on his mobile phone of Moshe posing in traditional attire alongside other rabbis. A rabbi is a spiritual leader, religious teacher and legal scholar. In the photograph, the once two-year-old ‘Baby Moshe’, whose footage of sobbing inconsolably after the attack drew global attention and moved millions, appears as a 20-year-old man. “He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi. Hopefully, he will return to India. That is our hope,” Kozlovsky told PTI on Wednesday. Nobody should go through what I have gone through: 26/11 survivor 'Baby Moshe' Moshe’s parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and mother Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when terrorists stormed the Chabad House, a centre that served the Jewish community here. Moshe’s nanny, Sandra Samuel, rescued him from the building and fled. He later moved to Israel to stay with his grandparents. He last visited Nariman House in 2018 alongside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. At present, the Nariman House building is undergoing renovation and is draped in green safety netting, making it difficult to identify from the outside. The only sign of it being a landmark here is the iron door usually found at the entrance of embassies. “Until November 26, 2008, this place primarily served as a centre for the Jewish community from India and abroad. Later, a decision was taken to convert part of it into a museum and turn this place into a beacon of peace,” Kozlovsky said. “You cannot let terrorists define and determine your life. So we need to open our gates,” he added. 18 years after 26/11 Mumbai attacks, memories and scars lives on The rabbi said that of the six floors, three floors will be for carrying out the activities of the Chabad House while the remaining three floors and the ground floor will be converted into a museum and a memorial to commemorate the victims who lost their lives in the terror attack here. “Even school children can come here,” Kozlovsky said, adding that work for raising funds has already begun and the construction work should be over in a year and a half. Kozlovsky said on the occasion of the 26/11 anniversary, a community prayer has been organised at the Chabad House here and many delegations are also expected on Thursday. Kozlovsky replaced Rabbi Chanoch Gechtman, who had succeeded Gavriel Holtzberg. Hailing from Jerusalem, Kozlovsky has been in charge of the activities in Nariman House since 2012. Less than a kilometre away from Nariman House stands Leopold Cafe, another landmark targeted during the 26/11 attacks. The iconic cafe, popular among foreign tourists, underwent repairs following the siege and was bustling with both locals and foreigners on Wednesday afternoon. While the establishment has moved past the tragedy, with staff reluctant to speak about it, visitors remain aware of its history. “I like the food here,” said Trish, a Hungarian national touring India who is visiting the eatery for the second time after reading about it in a travel guide. Sipping her juice, she added that she knew about the 2008 terror attack at the cafe, having read about it on the internet.

articles.title: Tata Trusts moves Bombay High Court against reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman of Tata Sons
articles.summary: Mumbai: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) filed suits in the Bombay High Court on Thursday against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore and RDTT will seek Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest. As per the suits, the September 17 decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company’s Articles of Association. The dispute follows N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman for another five years at the September 17 board meeting. Tata Sons listing will change way of working, Trusts will engage with regulators: Noel Tata The two trusts voted on Wednesday night to pass the resolutions to move HC as there was a lack of any satisfactory replies to the communications sent by them since September 17. The immediate relief being sought is to ensure that the chairman during the November 30 meeting is prevented from exercising his casting vote in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors. Tata Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata, holds around 66 per cent of Tata Sons and has challenged the board resolution passed on September 17. In its September 20 statement, the Trusts said the resolution was not validly passed and had “no legal effect”. At the centre of the dispute are Tata Sons’ Articles of Association (AoA) and special rights given to Trusts-nominated directors. It has two nominee directors on its board -- Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan. On September 17, Noel Tata voted against Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, while Venu Srinivasan supported it. As per Trusts, both nominated directors were required to support the decision. In its statement issued in September, the Trusts said the AoA of Tata Sons provide that no decision can be taken unless it has the affirmative support of at least a majority of the Directors nominated by the Tata Trusts. “This is a separate condition under the AoA,” it said, pointing out that the AoA does not leave any decision of the board to a mere head count of directors.

The flowering season is expected to continue into early December. The initiative is part of the government’s effort to extend Kashmir’s tourism season. Cubbon Park to bloom with 15 lakh flowers during 13-day festival from November 25 “We have been trying to increase our tourism season,” Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said while inaugurating the garden on October 23. The attraction has also drawn appreciation from visitors. Pooja, a tourist from Delhi, who visited the garden said: “We weren’t expecting to see the gardens today. We didn’t know about them. And it’s absolutely gorgeous.” The garden’s development involves the SK University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), which is working on varieties suited to local climatic conditions. Javed Masood Dar, the university official in charge of the garden, said staggered plantation was being used to prolong flowering. “We are using a staggering plantation, which could potentially stretching the floral season to over a month and a half,” Dar said. The university is also experimenting with different varieties, including multiflora chrysanthemums, some of which can be planted directly in the ground under Kashmir’s climatic conditions. The initiative could have implications beyond tourism, an official at the SKUAST said. Local propagation of chrysanthemums may encourage ornamental floriculture, creating opportunities for nurseries, growers and small entrepreneurs. “For Kashmir’s tourism-dependent businesses, attractions during quieter months could help sustain activity after the summer rush,” said a tour operator in Srinagar. He said hotels, transport operators, restaurants and local vendors are among those affected by seasonal fluctuations in visitor arrivals. However, the reported popularity of the garden does not establish how many visitors travelled to Srinagar specifically to see the flowers or whether it generated additional hotel bookings and longer stays. The Tulip Garden has acquired a distinct identity for spring. Whether chrysanthemums can create a similar attraction for autumn will depend on sustained visitor interest and the economic activity they generate.

articles.title: US officials divided over Chinese spying allegations following Jensen Huang's return
articles.summary: Days after President Donald Trump declared Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not a security threat to the United States, a central question remains unanswered: was the woman Huang was having an affair with a Chinese spy? Senior US national security officials, including at the White House, FBI and the CIA, have debated that question in recent days in an effort to determine if Alice Huang — a former executive at a major Nvidia customer — was working for or passing information to China's premier spy agency, according to five people familiar with the matter, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. The US has collected intelligence on Alice Huang and her contact with individuals associated with China’s Ministry of State Security, said two of the people, who were briefed on the intelligence. That intelligence has been described for months in reports from several intelligence agencies, including the CIA, the people said. US finds no evidence of China asking Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO: Report Key officials, including those at the FBI, the CIA and Marco Rubio, Trump's national security advisor and secretary of state, have — while agreeing on the underlying facts — taken different positions on the meaning of the information gathered by US spy agencies. Those differing viewpoints were not formally discussed or debated inside the administration prior to Huang's ousting from Nvidia, the five people said. The interpretation of the facts is important for understanding Trump's decision to push for Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia, three of the people said. The intelligence will likely be central to any congressional investigation into Nvidia and the president’s actions. Reuters could not determine the details of the intelligence reports. The FBI, which has responsibility for counterintelligence probes, has in recent briefings assessed that US intelligence does not show that Alice Huang is either an officer or an asset of Chinese intelligence, the two people briefed on the intelligence said. The CIA's view is more nuanced. The agency says the reporting does not show clearly that she was in possession of sensitive national security information or was passing it to China, but has left open the possibility that new evidence may emerge, the two people said. Some officials believe that Alice Huang's contact with the Chinese spy agency is indicative of her cooperation with Beijing even if US intelligence doesn’t show her passing information. A classified memo written by Rubio earlier this year indicated that the MSS had recruited Huang, potentially as an asset, according to an earlier New York Times report. The intelligence reports were held closely inside the intelligence community and among cabinet officials. They were not shared with Congress, the two people said. The White House, CIA, FBI and State Department declined to comment. Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologized, but has not publicly addressed the alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful. Intelligence not widely shared The different interpretations of US intelligence highlight what current and former intelligence officials say has become a problem for the Trump administration: classified information is now less widely shared and debated inside the intelligence community. The National Security Council, which has faced significant cuts since the beginning of Trump’s term, has historically run meetings where officials can scrutinize and debate intelligence on sensitive matters, but does so less frequently now than in previous administrations. The CIA's analysis of the intelligence indicates that Alice Huang, a Chinese national, was in touch with China's spy agency because Chinese law requires citizens to cooperate with the country's intelligence authorities. When the New York Times broke the news about that memo earlier this month, it caused uproar inside the administration and among board members of Nvidia who questioned whether Huang knew he was having an affair with someone who was passing information to China, according to two people familiar with the the conversations. Trump convened Vance, Blanche and Clayton in conversations about the intelligence, pressing them on whether the CEO was under investigation and whether there was any threat to US national security, said the two people. Blanche told Vance that Huang posed no threat, as Reuters has previously reported. Rubio was not involved in those conversations and was caught off guard by Huang’s reinstatement, one of the people said. The State Department did not respond to questions about Rubio's involvement in the conversations.

articles.title: IBM ends US visa sponsorship, gives H-1B workers three weeks to relocate or leave company
articles.summary: Following International Business Machines ' (IBM) decision to discontinue H-1B visa and employment-based Green Card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting division in the United States (US) , affected employees have been given three weeks to choose between relocating to another country for a new role within the company or leaving, according to a report by Rest of World. Employees who do not opt for relocation will receive three months' severance, with December 31, 2026, set as their last working day, Sunguk Moon, CEO of anonymous workplace forum Blind, told Rest of World . The development comes after IBM announced that it would discontinue visa and Green Card sponsorship for the majority of roles in IBM Consulting, its largest business division. IBM to end H-1B, Green Card sponsorship for most consulting roles. Who will be affected and how? The decision could affect foreign professionals who depend on employer sponsorship to continue working in the US. While IBM has offered employees the option of continuing their careers from overseas offices, the availability of suitable positions, differences in compensation and the personal costs of relocating could make the choice difficult for many. Most overseas openings are in India The relocation option appears to be concentrated largely in India. On November 19, IBM's careers portal listed 1,278 consulting positions outside the US, of which 1,125 were in India. Singapore had 23 openings and the United Kingdom had 18. The US, meanwhile, had 89 listed positions. The figures indicate that India could be a major destination for employees considering an internal transfer. However, IBM has not disclosed how many employees are affected by the decision or whether the available vacancies are suitable for their existing roles and experience. Relocation could also come with a significant financial impact. An IBM employee, writing anonymously on Blind, said moving to India could result in an approximately 80 per cent reduction in salary. Beyond compensation, moving countries could affect employees' professional networks, career progression and access to leadership opportunities. Explained | What are H-1B visas for skilled workers and what changes loom? Zakaria Laaraj, founder of consultancy Global New Ventures, told Rest of World that relocation does not necessarily guarantee continued engagement or equal access to professional opportunities. He said the viability of such an offer would depend on factors including an employee's tenure, available positions, immigration requirements and compensation. What IBM says about ending visa sponsorship IBM has attributed the decision to changes in the availability of skilled workers and the requirements of its clients. "IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages," an IBM spokesperson told Rest of World. The spokesperson added that the company's participation in these programmes had been declining for several years. "As skill availability and client need have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting," the spokesperson said. US to tighten visa regulations: What it means for foreign students and journalists IBM Consulting employs more than 1,50,000 people globally. However, the company has not disclosed the number of employees who will be affected by the revised policy or provided details of how the transition will be handled across different locations. The decision also comes against the backdrop of a decline in IBM's H-1B petition approvals. Federal immigration records show that the company received just over 1,600 approvals in fiscal year 2026, compared with more than 2,000 in FY2025 and nearly 3,000 in FY2024. US immigration restrictions add to uncertainty IBM's move comes as technology companies navigate tighter scrutiny of foreign-worker hiring under President Donald Trump's administration. In September 2025, the White House announced a one-time USD 100,000 fee on certain new H-1B visa applications. The measure has since faced legal challenges. The administration has also proposed changes to the annual H-1B selection process that would give greater weight to higher-paid applicants. More recently, the US Department of Labor suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several major IT outsourcing companies from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) process, according to Reuters. These developments have added to the uncertainty faced by foreign professionals seeking to establish long-term careers in the US.

articles.summary: Idukki (Keralam): While many people in Chinnakanal in this hill district fear the wild elephant, Chakkakomban, 65-year-old Mariyamma believes the animal keeps thieves away from her house. Living alone in her small home at B L Ram, she considers the elephant, which often passes by her house, a protector. "I am not afraid of him. Because the elephant comes this way, I feel thieves will not come here," says Mariyamma, who is used to the visits of Chakkakomban. Sometimes, people call her to warn that the elephant is on its way and ask her to switch on the lights. #WATCH | Keralam | Wild elephant Chakkakomban tranquillised on Wednesday under the Forest Department’s operation by a 140-member team, including veterinary doctors and Rapid Response Team personnel. The elephant will be fitted with a radio collar to enable continuous tracking… pic.twitter.com/8KUNE5CRPk — ANI (@ANI) November 25, 2026 She does so, closes the doors and goes to sleep. Keralam: Chakkakomban mission begins in Idukki, 140-member team deployed to tranquilise wild elephant By the next morning, the elephant would have left, and she can see the path it took. "I switch on the lights, close the door and sleep. When I wake up in the morning, I can see the path taken by the elephant. I have no problem staying alone. I feel Chakkakomban is there to protect me," she told a news channel. The route taken by the elephant passes behind her house and through a nearby plot. Local people often refer to it as the route through the 'Military House', a name linked to her husband, Subedar Rajan, who served in the Indian Army. The elephant is a familiar visitor to this stretch, and its movement through the property has become part of the area’s daily life. He earned the name Chakkakomban because of his fondness for jackfruit, which he frequently seeks out in human settlements. Mariyamma came to Chinnakanal from Tamil Nadu with her father when she was just 12. More than five decades later, she continues to live in the same region. At 65, she stays alone in her small house, but says she has learnt to live without fear. She has two granddaughters, both married, who visit her every week. She also has many memories of travelling to different parts of the country with her husband during his years in the Army. The stories and experiences from those days continue to give her courage. "People tell me that my husband was in the military and that I should not be afraid. But what can I do by being afraid? Where can I go? I have nowhere else to go. I have to live here and die here," she said. Her faith in the elephant comes at a time when Chakkakomban has become the centre of a debate over human-elephant conflict in Chinnakanal. The forest department has been trying to capture the elephant and fit it with a radio collar to monitor its movements. A day-long operation on Wednesday ended without success after rain and thick fog forced forest officials to call it off. The proposed move to capture Chakkakomban and another wild elephant, Murivali, has also drawn opposition from environmental groups. The Co-Existence Collective, a group of environmental organisations, has submitted an urgent petition to the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, seeking an immediate halt to the operation. The group has called for independent scientific, ecological and veterinary studies before any attempt is made to capture or relocate the elephants. It has also sought the restoration of elephant corridors and water sources in Chinnakanal, along with an inquiry into human deaths and the use of firecrackers and explosives to drive elephants away. The petition also suggests measures such as trenches and early warning systems to reduce conflict between people and elephants.

'Good luck more than anything': John Wright on discovering a young Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: Christchurch: An image that went viral earlier this month was when former Mumbai Indians’ head coach John Wright caught up with his greatest discovery Jasprit Bumrah during the game between India A and New Zealand A in Lincoln, a suburb southwest of Christchurch. It was Wright who spotted Bumrah first duringight a Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy game between Gujarat and Mumbai in Motera while on a scouting programme in 2013, and after a chat with Parthiv Patel he immediately recommended the MI management to rope in the then 19-year-old. The pacer with a gingerly run-up and unique slingy action has now gone on to become one of the best all-format bowlers in the world. And Bumrah still shares a strong bond with the man who opened the window of opportunity for him. “Oh, well, it was good luck more than anything,” gushed Wright when quizzed about the meeting on Wednesday. The New Zealand great, India’s first-ever foreign coach between November 2000 and April 2005, said he spotted something special the moment he saw Bumrah. “It was 2013 and I’d just got the opportunity to coach the Mumbai Indians with Anil Kumble. So I went up to the West Zone, for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. And there were two games going on at that stage and I watched both. Then I wandered back to the game between Mumbai and Gujarat. It was only about six or seven overs to go. Jasprit Bumrah: India's trump card against New Zealand in the race to qualify for the World Test Championship final “Mumbai were going to win. They only had a few runs to get. But there was this kid who bowled from that end. He ran in and I watched him bowl an over and they were all yorkers. He had a bit of pace because one of them hit the bowler's footmarks and the ball took off and went for four byes. I thought, wow, the kid's got a bit of pace too. So I hung around and watched the other over. “Then he came on again and bowled another over. And he bowled another six yorkers. That's all he tried to bowl. So at the end of the game I wandered over to Parthiv Patel, who's a judge that I really respect. He was captain of Gujarat. I said ‘who's that bloke there?’ Parthiv gave him a very positive recommendation. Wright immediately dialled Rahul Sanghvi, Director of Cricket at Mumbai Indians, and ensured Bumrah was signed before the auction. The rest, as they say, is history with Bumrah instrumental in MI winning five IPL crowns as well as two T20 World Cups for India. IPL auction 2027 | Ben Stokes, David Warner among 1,220 players to register Wright said the moment batting great Sachin Tendulkar spoke highly of Bumrah he knew he’d made the right call. “He (Bumrah) was always special. When we signed him, we went to RCB. It was our first game and we had nets. I made him bowl to Sachin in the first nets we had. And at the end of the nets, Sachin came over to me and said ‘Who's that over there?’ And I said ‘Oh, that's a young lad called Bumrah.’ He said ‘Oh John, he’s very hard to pick up. That's when I did a jig for joy.” “You can pick someone and provide an opportunity. But then it's really up to the individual cricketer of what they’re going to make of that opportunity. And Jasprit, from my experience, is intelligent. I think he's quite humble. He's got an aptitude to learn. The most unique thing about him is the action. He's made the most of his opportunities. Someone would have found him at some stage. But I’m thrilled for the guy because he's been a great bowler and is a great bowler.” India vs New Zealand | 'There's no pattern': Morne Morkel on struggle to pick 20 wickets Talent scouting is huge in IPL nowadays given the amount of cricket that takes place, not just in India but across the world too. When asked what attributes a good scout needs to have, Wright felt intuition is very important. “It probably boils down to an eye. I'm not too sure, but for me personally, sometimes it can just be one shot or the way the ball bounces off the wicket. And then it arouses interest where you see something that's a little bit different or maybe a bit special or something. “With Hardik (Pandya) it was one shot, Bumrah we've talked about. The really good ones stand out. Sometimes it's a little bit of luck. I don't think it's an exact art. Sometimes you just hope you're lucky. But for me, I always like people who do well when the pressure is on. And I particularly notice more in the game situation than anything else. People who can perform when maybe the game's on the line will make a difference. Because sometimes that means that the temperament might be all right. And hunger is quite a big factor too.” Wright was all praise for IPL for constantly providing opportunities for domestic talents to make it big. “What I do think is fantastic with IPL is that everyone is now looking for the best talent. And that's just so great for kids growing up in India. And knowing that if they can get an opportunity to play at first-class level, there's going to be a whole lot of people looking at them to maybe give them that opportunity which can make a huge difference to their lives personally and their family. I think that that's one of the great things that's happened with IPL. You know there's no traditional barriers anymore. articles.summary: Kochi: The Kerala High Court has permitted a minor rape victim to undergo medical termination of her over 27-week pregnancy , even though the medical board said the procedure could result in her death, as the girl was unwilling to continue until the 32 weeks suggested by the doctors. Justice Harisankar V Menon said that since the victim is a minor who is pursuing her studies, "her wish also requires to be given utmost sanctity". "Therefore, taking note of the factual and legal position, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner requires to be immediately allowed," the court said. The medical board constituted on the court's orders had examined the girl and given a report stating that terminating the pregnancy at the current stage carried the increased risk of excessive haemorrhage, retained placenta, uterine rupture, premature rupture of membranes, high chances of infection, and anaesthetic risks including cardiac arrest and even death of the mother. Kerala High Court allows pregnancy termination of 15-year-old sexual assault victim The board had also opined that the procedure could adversely affect the girl's future pregnancies too. As the girl was unwilling to continue with the pregnancy, the court ordered the state government to make the arrangements for the termination of the pregnancy and to carry out the same without any delay after getting an undertaking from the victim regarding her willingness for the procedure. "If, in the event, the child (baby) survives the termination of the pregnancy, the state shall provide appropriate measures and standard neonatal care," the court said. It also said that if the victim did not want the baby, she shall unconditionally surrender the infant to a childcare institution or specialised adoption agency for being placed in adoption. The court said that if the baby does not survive, the hospital shall preserve tissues and blood samples of the foetus for necessary medical tests, including DNA, fingerprinting, and mapping, since an FIR has been registered.

articles.title: India vs New Zealand | 'There's no pattern': Morne Morkel on struggle to pick 20 wickets
articles.summary: Christchurch: For two consecutive Tests now, India have had the opposition under the mat but they haven’t been able to enforce a result with both games ending up in draws that has significantly hurt their scoring in the World Test Championship table. Although the pitches in both the matches — the first being the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground in Colombo in late August and the second at Basin Reserve in Wellington last week — had flattened out considerably making batting easy and bowling a real hard task, the lack of cutting edge, at times, was visible. In Colombo, India looked on course for 2-0 whitewash when they reduced Sri Lanka to 229/6 at stumps on the fourth day after asking the hosts to follow-on. Just ahead by 16 runs but only four wickets in hand, Sri Lanka were staring down the barrel but overnight batter Sonal Dinusha scored an unbeaten 133 off 264 balls and forged two key partnerships with Keshara Nuwantha (46, 150b) and Lahiru Kumara (12, 90b) to defy India. India vs New Zealand 2nd Test preview| With WTC points at stake visitors eye victory at Christchurch In Wellington, it was Daryl Mitchell (49 n.o., 186b), Tom Blundell (15, 54b) and Glenn Phillips (26 n.o., 126b) who batted with extreme discipline to ensure India didn’t nick the game despite bowling their hearts out on a largely unresponsive surface. It’s in moments and days like these that teams need a moment of magic or slice of luck to swing the momentum their way and India could find neither. When asked if India’s inability to bowl out sides or the failure to get them out quickly is becoming a matter of concern, bowling coach Morne Morkel said his bowlers tried as hard as they could. “To be honest with you, there's no pattern sort of standing out. Every Test match, there was a difference, if you do the review, if you look at, you know, the whys that potentially didn’t happen, there's a different thing that pops out. So it's almost like, prepare for one thing, try to make one area a little better,” the South African said on the eve of the second Test starting against New Zealand on Friday. India vs New Zealand | Matt Henry expects another 'belter' of a pitch at Christchurch “So I think that's the beauty about the game. If you look at the week leading up to the last Test match, raining, you know, we saw the wicket, it was a nice amount of grass cover. It looked like it was going to be also a surface that will make a couple of dents, and if those dents get a little bit harder, they create a bit of up and down which we didn't see. Not a lot of balls kept low. There's not a lot of variation off the surface. Like I said, it's been a challenging sort of period that we're also trying to get better at and put our finger on. But I think at the moment things are going the way we would like.” Will Brar play? India skipper Shubman Gill, after the opening Test, said the team for the second too will likely be the same XI. When asked if Gurnoor Brar could replace the disappointing Anshul Kamboj, Morkel said it’s up to the team management. “With Gurnoor, there's a lot of excitement about him since he's joined the Indian team with his pace and bounce. I think he's a guy that will be well-suited to the conditions here. We'll see how it goes, and the pitch. “Gurnoor has been knocking on the door. He's doing all the right things. But, again, the selection for him as a player is something that I can’t (comment). He needs to just make sure he's ready when he gets the opportunity. I think a lot of times, we think we want that opportunity. We want to be close, and as a bowler, you can get distracted. When he gets his opportunity, which is we never know. My job is to make sure he's 100% ready when he gets that opportunity.”

articles.summary: Tamil Nadu has accused Karnataka of drawing more than its allocated share of Cauvery water during the current distress year, saying the shortfall is affecting farmers in the state's delta region. The state raised the objection at a meeting of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) in New Delhi on November 25. In a dissent note submitted at the authority's 62nd meeting, Tamil Nadu questioned the decisions taken by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the CWMA, saying they did not follow the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal's Final Award or the Supreme Court's judgement. It also said the decisions did not reflect the data collected by the authorities. Tamil Nadu argued that the Supreme Court's judgement required the allocated shares of all basin states to be reduced proportionately during distress years. Although the deficit percentage had been assessed and Tamil Nadu's pro-rata share at Biligundulu calculated, Karnataka had not been directed to release the corresponding quantity of water, Tamil Nadu said. The state also disputed the method used to calculate the distress percentage. It maintained that the deficit must be determined through an assessment of water yield, as prescribed in the Union government's Gazette notification dated June 1, 2018. Since this method had not been followed, Karnataka was being allowed to draw more than its due share, leaving farmers in the Cauvery delta to bear the consequences, the dissent note said. Tamil Nadu further criticised the authorities for taking what it described as ad hoc decisions based on vague assessments of ground realities, rather than following the prescribed methodology. It said its objections to the calculation of the distress percentage remained unchanged. The meeting was held in hybrid mode at the CWMA's committee room in New Delhi. Piyush Singh, who took additional charge as the authority's chairman after SK Haldar retired, chaired the meeting. Tamil Nadu was represented by Prasanth Vadanare, Secretary of the Water Resources Department, and Subramanian, chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell. The objection comes days after the Supreme Court rejected Tamil Nadu's applications seeking directions to Karnataka to release additional Cauvery water to make up for the alleged shortfall. On November 20, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh dismissed the applications, which cited the impact of water scarcity on farmers and crops. Tamil Nadu had filed two applications seeking the immediate release of its due share of Cauvery water.

Karnataka HC quashes FIR over alleged tampering in 2023 Sringeri election
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against former BJP MLA DN Jeevaraj and two election officials over alleged tampering with postal ballots in the 2023 Sringeri Assembly election. The court held that the complaint, filed nearly three years after the original counting, was too delayed to sustain the prosecution. In an order passed on November 21, Justice M Nagaprasanna set aside the FIR registered by Chikkamagaluru Town Police against Jeevaraj, former Deputy Commissioner KN Ramesh and Returning Officer TR Vedamurthy. The case involved allegations of forgery, criminal conspiracy and violations of the Representation of the People Act (1951). The complaint was filed on May 3, 2026, by Sudhir Kumar Murolli, an election agent and authorised representative of Congress candidate TD Rajegowda. It alleged that postal ballots had been tampered with after the original counting on May 13, 2023, including ballots that had been cast in Rajegowda's favour. The complaint also alleged that ballot box seals had been removed and ballot paper account sheets altered to secure an electoral advantage. The complaint came hours after a recount ordered by the High Court resulted in Jeevaraj being declared the winner of the Sringeri constituency. The original result had gone in Rajegowda's favour by a margin of 201 votes, with 279 postal ballots rejected. Jeevaraj had challenged the election result through an election petition. On April 6, 2026, the High Court partly allowed his petition and directed the Returning Officer to re-verify the 279 rejected postal ballots and recount all postal ballots. The recount was completed on May 2, following which Jeevaraj was declared elected. The Supreme Court subsequently stayed the operation of the revised result, and Rajegowda continues as the MLA under its interim order. The three accused approached the High Court seeking to quash the criminal case. They argued that the complaint was an attempt to reopen matters already considered in the election petition and that the nearly three-year gap between the original counting and the complaint was unexplained. They also contended that an election agent could not initiate a private complaint for offences under the Representation of the People Act. The High Court did not accept the argument that election-related criminal complaints could only be taken to the Election Commission or an election officer. Referring to the relevant legal provisions and Supreme Court judgments, Justice Nagaprasanna said a private complaint could be maintained in appropriate circumstances. However, the court found the delay in this case significant. It noted that the ballot boxes had remained sealed in strong rooms under police security from May 13, 2023, until they were opened for the recount in May 2026. It also observed that Murolli could have approached the authorities in 2023 itself if he suspected irregularities in the original counting. The court said the complaint had been filed only after the recount went against Rajegowda and Jeevaraj was declared the winner. It held that the timing and the unexplained delay made the criminal proceedings unsustainable. “With the declaration of the results after recounting in which the candidate loses and accused No.2 is declared as a winning candidate, investigation by the jurisdictional police on a complaint cannot emerge. It is undoubtedly hit by delay,” the court said. It also observed that the delay had led to embellishments in the complaint. The court said vague and general allegations made after such a long interval could not be used to subject the accused to investigation or trial. It further questioned the implication of prosecuting election officials over the declaration of Rajegowda as the returned candidate, when the alleged irregularities in the original counting had not been challenged at the time. The FIR invoked sections 143, 465, 468, 471, 120B and 149 of the Indian Penal Code, along with section 136 of the Representation of the People Act.
